title: 15 YouTube Shorts Ideas, Each a Real AI Short
summary: 15 YouTube Shorts ideas you can copy, each shown as a real AI short: reactions, spoken lines, surreal worlds and repeatable formats, with how to make them.
body_markdown:
### What should I make a YouTube Short about?


Pick one small moment you can describe in a sentence, such as a reaction, a spoken opinion or one strange picture. A single idea fits the format better than a story squeezed down, and it is easier to repeat as a series.


### What are easy YouTube Shorts ideas for beginners?


The easiest ideas need one image and one action, such as a character smiling, a cloud drifting over a still scene or a cartoon villain grinning. With no script, one location and one movement, there is little that can go wrong.


### How long should a YouTube Short be?


YouTube allows Shorts of up to 3 minutes, and it publishes no single best length. Flick's own experiments ran 5 to 10 seconds, which is enough for one reaction or one spoken line, so let the idea set the length.


### What aspect ratio does a YouTube Short need?


YouTube treats a video as a Short when it is square or vertical and up to 3 minutes long, and wider videos stay long-form. Set a Flick project to 9:16 before you generate, because a widescreen clip will not count as a Short.


### Can I make YouTube Shorts with AI?


Yes. In Flick you can generate an image, animate it, add a voice and export the video from one canvas, starting on free credits. You get 100 credits when you sign up and 100 credits every week, and models such as Kling 3.0 Pro need the Standard plan ($20 a month).


### Do I have to label AI-generated YouTube Shorts?


YouTube[requires creators to disclose AI-generated or altered content that seems realistic](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491) , and it does not require this for clearly unrealistic content such as animation. A cartoon Short usually needs no label, while a realistic person or event does.


### Can I use these YouTube Shorts ideas for my own channel?


Yes, an idea is free to borrow as a starting point. The original films, characters and images belong to the filmmaker who made them, so generate your own picture rather than reposting theirs.
